transcript: Free Shakespeare in the park is back with a starry production of Twelfth Night to reopen the renovated Delacorte Theater. This was our second attempt at attending the show after being rained out a few weeks ago, and it was well worth the wait. Despite it being one of Shakespeare's most well known comedies, this production of Twelfth Night as directed by Saheem Ali doesn't reinvent the wheel, but leans into the inherent joys of comedy and live performance. Performed in one act, integrating live music, and boasting a colorfully slick design, this has all the ingredients for a crowd-pleaser. Throw in a great cast including folks like Lupita Nyong’o, Sandra Oh, Peter Dinklage, and Jesse Tyler Ferguson, and the result is a whimsical experience that could only happen under the stars in Central Park. Across the board, the performances are solid from the ensemble to the leading players, and the big names here don't overshadow the story they’re telling. Everyone's just having fun and the energy is contagious. I was especially charmed by Mavolio’s scene with the letter — Peter Dinklage's hilarious performance plus some really playful prop work by his deceivers made the scene a highlight, for sure. As a production of Twelfth Night, this isn't the most daring or nuanced version, but you can't deny that it's a good time — and for me, that was more than enough. With just about a week left in the run, I think getting tickets is more difficult than ever, but if you have a chance to go, you will not regret it. With that, another program for my collection.
